title: Pakistan Climate Change Act, 2017 (Act No. X of 2017)
evidence: Header of the Act in the Pakistan Code PDF: "ACT NO. X OF 2017 [29th March, 2017]"; s. 1(3): "It shall come into force at once." Opened https://pakistancode.gov.pk/pdffiles/administrator35e25fe56389d477d508cdf8a693e868.pdf on 2026-11-02.
notes: The Pakistan Code listing page gives the promulgation date as March 31 2017; the Act's own header says 29th March, 2017, and that date is used (it agrees with the brief). Establishes the Pakistan Climate Change Council and Authority; creates no reporting duty on companies. Link only: the only publisher source opened (Pakistan Code) has verdict permission requested (PK-PAKISTANCODE-CONSOLIDATED), so no text is stored. Pakistan Code serves one revised text per law, with no earlier versions; the Gazette (https://drs.molaw.gov.pk/Home, https://www.egazette.gov.pk) and the National Assembly site (https://na.gov.pk) were not reachable from the cloud address. English is the language the law is enacted in, so no translation was looked for; the Pakistan Code has an Urdu interface (https://pakistancode.gov.pk/english/UHyrdu.php), and the per-law Urdu text was not examined.

title: Petroleum Products (Petroleum Levy) and Climate Support Levy Ordinance, 1961 (Ordinance No. XXV of 1961), s. 3(4) Climate Support Levy
citation: Ordinance No. XXV of 1961, s. 3(4) as inserted by the Finance Act, 2025 (Act No. XIX of 2025), s. 3
evidence: No official page opened states the date. s. 3(4) in the Pakistan Code PDF: "A Climate Support Levy shall be levied at the rate of two rupees and fifty paisa (Rs. 2.5) per liter on Motor Spirit and High Speed Diesel for Financial Year 2025-26, which shall be enhanced to five rupees per liter for Financial Year 2026-27." Footnote: "Ins. by the Finance Act, 2025 (Act No. XIX of 2025), s.3." Opened https://pakistancode.gov.pk/pdffiles/administrator1bc3ad732b91e47508abf826f2840d15.pdf on 2026-11-02.
notes: The Finance Act 2025 itself (na.gov.pk) could not be opened, and it is not in the Pakistan Code list, so its commencement clause was not read; press reports give 2025-07-01 but no official page opened states it, so in_force is null. The Ordinance amended by s. 3 is this entry. The text confirms the Rs 2.5 per litre rate for 2025-26 and Rs 5 for 2026-27 on motor spirit, high speed diesel and furnace oil. Press reports of a later change in rate were not checked against an official page. No emissions trading scheme exists; the Carbon Market Policy Guidelines 2024 are policy and not stored. title: Competition Act, 2010 (Act No. XIX of 2010), s. 10 deceptive marketing practices
evidence: Header of the Act in the Pakistan Code PDF: "ACT NO. XIX OF 2010 [6th October, 2010]"; s. 1(4): "It shall come into force at once." Opened https://pakistancode.gov.pk/pdffiles/administratore1b5ab79c2c1975670e6aa7fe57e57d6.pdf on 2026-11-02.
notes: The Pakistan Code listing page gives Oct 13 2010; the Act's header says 6th October, 2010, and that date is used. Section 10(2)(b) covers false or misleading information to consumers about the character, method or place of production, properties or quality of goods, and (c) false comparison in advertising; the section does not mention environmental claims. There is no federal consumer protection act; the Punjab Consumer Protection Act 2005 is not in scope and was not opened. title: State Bank of Pakistan SH&SFD Circular No. 07 of 2025: Regulatory Framework for Effective Management of Climate-related Financial Risks
evidence: Circular page (opened with headless Chromium on 2026-11-02; curl gets HTTP 403): dated "December 26, 2025"; "All FIs shall ensure the compliance to the framework by June 30, 2029. For the purpose, FIs are required to submit, board-approved, time-bound implementation plans and targets to SBP by September 30, 2026." The circular has no commencement clause, so its issue date is used.
notes: Addressed to all banks, DFIs and microfinance banks. Kept in F6: it is a binding supervisory framework on climate risk governance and risk management for financial institutions (like the UK FCA row), not a company disclosure rule (the Annexure has no disclosure requirement: a search of its text for the word found none) and not a claims rule, so F1 and F7 fit worse. Link only: PK-SBP-ADOPTED has verdict permission requested. Annexure: https://www.sbp.org.pk/assets/documents/circulars/SHSFD-2025-C7-Annex.pdf (curl HTTP 200, PDF). English only.
